recipes.name: Almond Flour Pancakes
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, melted and cooled

steps.text: Preheat a non-stick griddle to 375 degrees F (185 degrees C). Lightly grease the cooking surface with butter.

Sift the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together into a mixing bowl. Mix the almond flour and sugar into the flour mixture until just blended. Stir the yogurt, eggs, and butter together in a separate bowl; add to the flour mixture, stirring only until just incorporated. The batter will be thick and airy.

Pour about 1/3 cup of the batter onto your preheated cooking surface, leaving space for the pancakes to expand. Cook until dry around the edges and bubbles have formed over the top, 2 to 3 minutes; turn and continue cooking until done in the middle and golden brown, another 1 to 2 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Almond Flour Pancakes
raw_recipe.description: These fluffy pancakes have a light texture and a great, slightly-nutty taste.

review.reviewBody: These were very good, however I did add some vanilla extract and some agave nectar. Otherwise I left everything the same. Very filling and yummy!

Had to place a star rating. Star rating is based on way too much salt for inedible pancakes and no vanilla extract for bland pancakes. I translated cups to grams being UK. I made substitutes as I saw fit but didn't alter the recipe significantly like others online do... White spelt flour for AP (AP tastes disgusting, spelt and other ancient grains flours taste nice), didn't have blanched almonds so ground roasted almonds in a spice grinder (be aware roasted almonds are drier than raw blanched almonds aka almond flour so absorbs less liquid), 59g/1/4 cup browned butter instead of butter (I was making ghee at the time), probably 1tbsp extra egg as sizes differ across countries, 3/8tsp flaky sea salt (instead of US kosher salt) is salty so reduce to 1/4tsp, 35g brown sugar instead of white for flavour (1tbsp brown sugar = 8g/1tbsp granulated sugar = 20g), added 1tsp mixed spices (cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves), 1/2tsp homemade vanilla extract (double strength), 2 splashes of almond extract for flavour (surprised it was missing from the original!) and lastly instead of 2 cups/450g yoghurt, I used leftover soured cream (85ml* 1/3 cup) , leftover double cream (heavy cream? 45-60ml* 3-4tbsp) and 190g*/heaping 3/4 cup Greek style soy yoghurt (total 320g = 1.4 cups), and 45ml/3-4tbsp whole milk to create a batter. Note I can't stomach raw yoghurt but pancakes benefit from the tang and the thickness so I dilution was necessary. Lastly the method omits resting the batter which I don't get. You should always rest pancake batter (30-60 minutes is the standard, 15 minutes works if pressed for time) so the flour absorbs water, raising agents get to work and in the end you get the "correct" pancake texture and flavouring - no gummy middle, no raw flour taste, airier and fluffier pancake, looks and taste cooked, what's not to like! As I say, I altered the recipe to get what I wanted - a light, fluffy, thick cake in a pan with oodles of flavour. Perfect for dressing up with maple syrup, good quality i.e. Bonne Maman chocolate and hazelnut spread (not Nutella!) or a drizzle of cream for dessert. Delicious.

Delicious and very fluffy! A great base recipe that you can spruce up however you like! I did make a few changes. The yogurt I had on hand was Icelandic yogurt, which is more sour than your average yogurt, and the consistency of Greek yogurt. Because of that, I used just under a cup of yogurt, and made up the difference with plain kefir. I also used more sugar than the recipe called for. I didn't measure, but it was about 2 Tbsp. I added about a tsp of vanilla extract, as well. I also used just under the cup of all purpose flour, and used about 1/4 c of wheat bran, to add some fiber and nutritional content. After making the first few, and finding that they were very fluffy, but still pretty tart, I added a mashed banana. It added a bit of moisture and sweetness, and they were perfect after that. I would suggest trying them before doing that. If you use regular yogurt and not Icelandic, they should be sweet enough without the banana, but with a slightly tart edge, like buttermilk pancakes. They do not bubble up as much and start to dry on the top side like regular wheat pancakes, so flip as soon as you see the edges taking shape. I love that the almond flour is low carb, and higher in fat and protein, and I feel less sluggish after these that all wheat pancakes, as a result. Thank you for a great, simple recipe!

This was a great recipe. The pancakes were light and tender. I have tried dozens of recipes and this is in my top 5. I will be making these again. I did make some changes. 
1 c whole sprouted whole wheat flour,
1 c almond flour,
1.5 c raw whole milk yogurt,
.5 c yogurt whey (when ever I strain yogurt I collect the whey to use int he future),
2 eggs,
1 tbsp raw pastured butter,
1 tsp baking soda,
1.5 tsp baking powder,
1 tbsp sucanat sugar,
1 tsp vanilla,
Dash of cinnamon,
.5 tsp kosher salt. 
I let the mixture rest for 1 hour before cooking. I used coconut oil on the griddle just because butter tends to burn and I didn't have any ghee. We had them with some fresh homemade butter and grade B maple syrup. YUM!

I’m going to get straight to the point. These are delicious, I’m in love with them. Remember, this is a base recipe: add vanilla, fruit, whatever. I personally added my homemade vanilla bean extract and doubled the sugar (I eat pancakes with very little syrup if any at all). I recommend using aluminum free baking powder or only using 1 1/4tsp. I think other reviews stating saltiness is actually the aluminum. If you use syrup like a most people you probably won’t notice it though. If you like thin pancakes spread it out as best as you can after pouring into a skillet/griddle and just flatten it after flipping.

I had high hopes for these. But the dough was too stiff and the flavor was too salty. I had to add 1/3c of almond milk to be able to spread the dough on the pan. Maybe it's because I used greek yougurt. I used agave syrup for sugar and grapeseed oil for butter. Overall I like the ingredients and the pancakes are very filling, so maybe I'll give them another try with less salt and the extra liquid.

All in all, this recipe was a success in our house. My husband and I really liked them and my kids thought they were tolerable, which I count as a success! My son is type 1 diabetic, so I'm always looking for lower carb recipes, so this was great for that. I added 1/2 tsp. of almond extract and 1/2 tsp. vanilla extract for extra flavor and swapped the 1 T. of sugar for 1.5 tsp. of stevia. I sprinkled unsweetened coconut flakes on top of mine and served with a little maple syrup & blueberries...a keeper!

Made a few changes by using coconut flour and cake flour. also used lactose free yogurt 6 oz and remaining non dairy yogurt drink by Califa. Sprinked cinnamon in the dry mix with date syrup in liquid for sweetener. My new go to pancake recipe..thank you for the inspiration with yogurt rather than milk (non dairy of course)
Really fluffy. A good compromise with half almond flour and half regular flour. Used regular 2% yogurt. Husband asked for more but only made half the amount since it's only 2 of us.

I used coconut oil instead of butter and used a 1/2 cup less yogurt but added 1/2 cup of milk because I used the thick Greek yogurt. Also cut the salt in half and they were plenty salty. True that you have to shape these by hand somewhat because they are too thick to spread out over the pan. They were tasty.
Great flavor, I added 1 cup of milk since the batter was very thick. They turned out great with the addition of the milk
Terrific recipe! Used einkorn white and almond flour. Light and fluffy.

Delicious! I used Chobani zero sugar yogurt and omitted the sugar. I heated up frozen berries (raspberries, blueberries, and blackberries) and poured over the top. No syrup needed. Thanks for the great recipe!
Nice, fluffy and soft pancakes. I'd use less salt next time. I added more sugar.
Yummy
Family loved it
Used a food processor - doubled the recipe
Turned out great! Fluffy. Only thing I would change next time is less salt in the batter

My husband & I really loved these Pancakes. I am a new diabetic and also new to using almond flour. I was overjoyed at the taste & texture and I followed the recipe as written. I am so very happy that even though I have to watch my carbs that I can still eat pancakes...oh I did thin the batter just a little with a splash of unsweetened almond milk... I feel these are a keeper and will be making them often !!!!!
the best recipe ever! I was so proud of my pancakes. thanks for sharing.
